fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the Cyber Risk Snapshot for the customer, review their security concerns and any recent incidents from intake, and schedule the assessment window with the admin contact who can grant read-only access.

Send prep instructions: customer should confirm which platforms hold business data (M365, Google Workspace, line-of-business apps), where backups live, and who the admin contacts are; gather any prior security assessments or insurance questionnaires.

Pre-work: prepare the six-domain review checklist (identity, endpoint, email, backup, network, policy/risk), stage evidence folders per domain, and pull domain authentication records for email posture.

Run the assessment: collect evidence across the six domains — MFA coverage and admin accounts (identity), endpoint protection and patch state (endpoint), SPF/DKIM/DMARC and mail rules (email), backup config/success/off-site (backup), firewall/Wi-Fi/remote access (network), and policies/incident history (policy/risk).
Score the snapshot: compute the numerical risk score with red/amber/green per-domain ratings, and select the top five critical actions with clear implementation guidance.
Walk through with the customer in a 30-minute session: review the risk score, the per-domain ratings, and the top five actions in plain English; answer leadership-level questions.
Deliver the closeout package: the Cyber Risk Snapshot report (leadership-ready), the top-five action sheet, and a recommended follow-on path (full assessment, managed security, or specific fixes).

triage: Confirm scope is the Cyber Risk Snapshot (lightweight six-domain review, read-only); if the customer reports an active incident, escalate to the appropriate emergency product.
Verify admin access to M365/cloud platforms and confirm who can speak to endpoint and backup state; request read-only access or guided sessions.
Gather baseline: tenant and domain names, user/device counts, backup platform, line-of-business apps, and any prior assessments or insurer questionnaires.

Create the ticket with product id cyber_risk_snapshot, the six domains, expected deliverables (snapshot report, top-five actions), exclusions (no changes), and assign a technician with broad security review experience.
Check prerequisites: data-gathering sessions booked and confirmation the customer understands this is assessment-only.
delivery: Identity domain: record MFA coverage across platforms, enumerate admin accounts, flag shared/generic credentials, and note separation-of-duties gaps with evidence.
Endpoint domain: record antivirus/EDR product and status, patch currency, disk encryption, and local admin rights for a representative device sample.
Email domain: pull SPF/DKIM/DMARC records, review anti-phishing policy presence, and scan mailbox forwarding rules for compromise indicators.
Backup domain: confirm platform, jobs running, recent success, retention, off-site copy, and whether restores were ever tested.
Network domain: review firewall posture, Wi-Fi security (WPA2/3, guest network), remote-access exposure (VPN vs RDP), and router/AP management access.
Policy/risk domain: note whether security policies exist (password, acceptable use, incident reporting), recent incidents, and insurance requirements.
Score and rank: compute the numerical risk score and per-domain red/amber/green ratings, then select the top five critical actions ordered by risk reduction and effort.
Technical verification: confirm every rating is evidence-backed, no changes were made, and no sensitive data appears in captures.
documentation: Produce the Cyber Risk Snapshot report: overall risk score, six domain ratings with traffic-light status, and a leadership-ready executive summary in plain English.
Include the top five critical actions with owner, effort, and implementation guidance for each.
Document per-domain evidence summaries (MFA coverage, endpoint posture, email/DNS, backup, network, policy) as the report's appendix.
Note the backup and MFA findings explicitly since they are the most common critical gaps for small businesses.
Security rule: never store credentials, backup keys, recovery codes, or personal data in the report or notes.
qa: Verify all whatIsIncluded items: six-domain review, numerical risk score with red/amber/green ratings, top five actions with guidance, leadership-ready report, and the 30-minute walkthrough.
Confirm the assessment was read-only and no system or policy changes were made.
Secret audit: confirm no credentials or sensitive data appear in deliverables.
Verify the risk scoring is consistent with prior snapshots so trends can be measured.
Flag follow-ups: critical gaps requiring action within 30 days, a full assessment recommendation if depth is needed, and any insurer-required controls.
closeout: Send the deliverables package: the snapshot report and top-five action sheet, with the walkthrough completed and acknowledged.
Recommend next steps based on findings: full_cybersecurity_assessment for depth, mct_secure_care or a monthly cyber plan for ongoing management, or specific fixes for quick wins.
Revoke any temporary access used for evidence gathering.
Record internal notes: baseline risk score, per-domain state, and evidence pointers so a future snapshot shows progress.
Schedule a 60-90 day follow-up to re-snapshot or check progress on the top five actions.

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the Full Cybersecurity Assessment, define the in-scope environment (users, devices, cloud platforms, servers, network), and schedule stakeholder interviews with owners, IT contacts, and key staff.

Send prep instructions: customer should gather current documentation (network diagram, device inventory, backup config, insurance questionnaire), confirm admin access for configuration review, and line up interview participants.
Pre-work: prepare the assessment plan across eight or more domains, stage evidence folders, assemble interview questions per role, and pull domain and tenant baseline data.
Run the assessment: conduct stakeholder interviews, review accessible system and platform configurations, collect evidence across all domains, and note both strengths and gaps with proof.
Score and document: build the detailed findings report with risk ratings and evidence for every finding, plus the executive summary for leadership.
Build the roadmap: create the phased remediation roadmap with priorities and estimated effort, ordered by risk reduction and dependency.
Walk through the findings with the customer in a Q&A session, then deliver the closeout package: findings report, executive summary, phased roadmap, and recommended first-phase engagement.

triage: Confirm scope is the Full Cybersecurity Assessment and that the customer wants depth across eight or more domains; if they need a faster lighter review, recommend cyber_risk_snapshot instead.
Confirm the environment scope: user/device counts, cloud platforms, servers, network gear, and any third-party systems, and identify the access needed for configuration review.
Gather baseline: existing documentation, prior assessments, insurance requirements, compliance drivers, and any known incidents.

Create the ticket with product id full_cybersecurity_assessment, the domain list, interview schedule, expected deliverables (findings report, executive summary, roadmap), and assign senior assessor(s).
Check prerequisites: interview participants confirmed, admin access arranged, and the assessment plan agreed with the customer.
delivery: Stakeholder interviews: conduct structured interviews with the owner, IT contact, and key staff covering how the business uses technology, what data matters most, and what keeps them up at night; record notes.
Identity domain review: enumerate accounts, roles, MFA coverage, legacy auth, stale accounts, and separation of duties across M365 and other platforms.
Endpoint domain review: for the fleet record EDR/AV status, patch currency, encryption, local admin rights, and device lifecycle state.
Email domain review: SPF/DKIM/DMARC, anti-phishing/anti-spam config, mailbox rules, and MFA on mailboxes.
Backup domain review: platform, job success history, retention, off-site copy, encryption of backups, and restore-test evidence.
Network domain review: firewall rules, Wi-Fi security and guest separation, remote-access exposure, segmentation, and device management access.
Policy and risk review: security policies, incident history, compliance requirements, and insurance controls; compare against common standards.
Additional domains as scoped (DLP, identity governance, cloud apps, physical security of IT) based on the customer's industry and data.
Score and document: rate each finding by severity with evidence, and verify every claim is traceable before it enters the report.
Technical verification: confirm no configuration changes were made (assessment only), and confirm access used was read-only.
documentation: Produce the detailed findings report: each finding with description, evidence, risk rating, and remediation guidance, organized by domain.
Produce the executive summary for board/leadership: the overall posture, the top risks in plain English, and the recommended investment priorities.
Build the phased remediation roadmap: phases with priorities, dependencies, and estimated effort, so the customer can execute in order.
Include the evidence index pointing to captured configurations, screenshots, and interview notes without embedding sensitive data.
Security rule: never include credentials, keys, backup recovery codes, or unredacted personal data in any deliverable; redact aggressively.
qa: Verify all whatIsIncluded items: eight-plus-domain coverage, stakeholder interviews, configuration review of accessible systems, findings report with risk ratings/evidence/remediation, executive summary, phased roadmap, and findings walkthrough with Q&A.
Confirm every finding in the report is backed by collected evidence and that severities are consistent.
Confirm the roadmap phases are ordered by risk reduction and are feasible in sequence.
Secret audit: confirm no credentials or sensitive data appear in deliverables or notes.
Flag follow-ups: urgent items from the first phase, and schedule the customer's decision point on which remediation work to start.
closeout: Deliver the closeout package: findings report, executive summary, phased roadmap, and evidence index; complete the walkthrough with Q&A.
Recommend the first-phase engagement mapped to the roadmap (e.g., mfa_enforcement_project, endpoint_protection_rollout, backup setup) and quote accordingly.
Revoke all temporary access granted for the assessment and confirm access state is unchanged.
Record internal notes: assessment baseline, key findings pointers, and the roadmap for future engagements.
Schedule a 90-day follow-up to review progress against the first roadmap phase.

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the M365 Security Assessment, verify the customer's tenant is in scope, and schedule the review with a Global Admin who can grant read-only access.
Send prep instructions: customer should confirm tenant admin access, list shared mailboxes and external sharing practices, and identify any known licensing gaps.
Pre-work: prepare the tenant review checklist (MFA/Conditional Access, roles, sharing, email protection, retention/backup/DLP, identity risk), and stage evidence folders.

Run the assessment: review the tenant's MFA and Conditional Access policies, admin role assignments, external sharing across SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams, email protection config, retention/backup/DLP posture, and identity risk settings.
Score and document: build the risk-ranked findings report with tenant-specific remediation guidance for each issue.
Walk through the findings with the customer: explain the tenant-specific issues in plain English and confirm the priority fixes.

Deliver the closeout package: the risk-ranked findings report with tenant-specific remediation guidance, plus a recommended follow-on quote (hardening project, licensing adjustments, or managed security).

triage: Confirm scope is the M365 Security Assessment for the specific tenant and that a Global Admin can provide access; if the customer is mid-breach, escalate to email/account compromise response.

Verify tenant admin access method (read-only delegated admin, break-glass with consent, or guided session) and confirm licensing allows the checks (P1/P2 where needed for Conditional Access and identity risk).
Gather baseline: tenant name, domains, license counts, shared mailboxes, external sharing behavior, and any prior M365 reviews.

Create the ticket with product id m365_security_assessment, expected deliverables (risk-ranked findings, remediation guidance), exclusions (no changes), and assign a technician with M365 security/Entra experience.
Check prerequisites: Global Admin session scheduled and confirmation the review is read-only.
delivery: MFA and Conditional Access review: in Entra admin center, document CA policies (which users/apps, report-only vs on), per-user MFA state, and security defaults; flag any gap where MFA is not enforced.
Role assignment review: enumerate Global Admins and all delegated admin roles (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Intune), flag excessive or stale assignments, and note separation-of-duties gaps.
External sharing review: check SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams external sharing settings (Anyone vs Existing guests vs new guests), list guest users, and note oversharing risk.
Email protection review: document anti-phishing policy impersonation protection, anti-spam thresholds, quarantine settings, and safe links/attachments state; pull SPF/DKIM/DMARC via MXToolbox.
Retention, backup, and DLP review: note retention policies, whether an external backup exists (M365 native is not backup), DLP policy presence, and eDiscovery permissions.
Identity risk review: check legacy auth enablement (basic auth protocols), risky sign-in detection (requires P2), stale/unused accounts, and self-service password reset configuration.
Score and document: rate findings by severity with tenant-specific evidence and write remediation guidance that names the exact setting path to change.
Technical verification: confirm all findings are tenant-specific and evidence-backed, no changes were made, and no sensitive data was captured.
documentation: Produce the risk-ranked findings report: each finding with severity, evidence, and tenant-specific remediation steps (exact admin path and setting).
Include the CA/MFA coverage summary, role inventory, external sharing status, email protection state, retention/backup/DLP posture, and identity risk findings.
Include the licensing notes: any checks that require P1/P2 licenses the tenant may not have, so the customer understands remediation prerequisites.
Document the SPF/DKIM/DMARC findings with exact recommended DNS record changes.
Security rule: never store tenant admin credentials, tokens, or recovery codes in the report or notes.
qa: Verify all whatIsIncluded items: CA/MFA review in the actual tenant, admin role audit, external sharing review across SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams, email protection review, retention/backup/DLP posture, identity risk review, and risk-ranked findings with remediation.
Confirm findings are tenant-specific (not generic) and traceable to collected evidence.
Confirm the assessment was read-only.
Secret audit: confirm no tenant secrets appear in deliverables.
Flag follow-ups: critical items (missing MFA, legacy auth, oversharing), licensing needs, and the recommended hardening engagement.
closeout: Send the deliverables package: risk-ranked findings report and remediation guidance; complete the walkthrough.
Recommend next steps: m365 hardening work (mfa_enforcement_project, email_security_hardening), the endpoint_protection_rollout if endpoints are exposed, or managed security for ongoing posture.
Revoke any temporary admin access and confirm tenant state is unchanged.
Record internal notes: tenant baseline, findings pointers, and licensing observations.
Schedule a 60-90 day follow-up to verify remediation progress.

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the Ransomware Readiness Review, and schedule the data-gathering with the admin who can speak to backups, MFA, endpoints, and recovery.
Send prep instructions: customer should confirm where backups run and whether they have ever tested a restore, and gather endpoint and M365 admin access.
Pre-work: prepare the readiness checklist across backups, MFA, endpoint protection, local admin rights, and recovery documentation.

Run the review: assess backup existence, success, off-site copy, and restore-testing; verify MFA coverage; review endpoint protection and patch state; check local admin rights; and review recovery documentation and incident-readiness.
Score and document: build the Ransomware Readiness Scorecard with prioritized hardening steps.
Walk through the scorecard with the customer: explain the biggest ransomware-relevant gaps (typically untested backups and missing MFA) and confirm the priority actions.
Deliver the closeout package: the scorecard, the prioritized hardening steps, and a recommended follow-on quote (backup setup, MFA enforcement, endpoint rollout).

triage: Confirm scope is the Ransomware Readiness Review; if the customer reports an active ransomware event, escalate to ransomware_first_response immediately.
Verify access to backup platforms, M365, and endpoint management; confirm who can describe the backup schedule.
Gather baseline: backup platform, MFA state if known, endpoint protection product, and any prior recovery testing.

Create the ticket with product id small_business_ransomware_readiness_review, expected deliverables (scorecard, hardening steps), exclusions (no changes), and assign a technician with backup and endpoint experience.
Check prerequisites: sessions booked and confirmation the review is read-only.
delivery: Backup assessment: confirm a backup solution exists, verify recent job success, check retention, confirm an off-site/immutable copy exists, and — critically — ask whether a restore has ever been tested and how recently.
MFA coverage review: verify MFA on email and critical cloud accounts, enumerate any accounts without MFA, and check admin accounts specifically.
Endpoint protection review: record the EDR/AV product and detection status, patch currency of OS and key apps, and note any devices with no protection.
Local admin rights review: identify workstations where users run as local admin, which dramatically increases ransomware blast radius.
Recovery documentation review: check whether the customer has documented recovery steps, a defined restore order, and an incident contact sheet.
Score and document: compute the readiness score and list prioritized hardening steps (test restore, enforce MFA, remove local admin, harden endpoints).
Technical verification: confirm all findings are evidence-backed and no changes were made.
documentation: Produce the Ransomware Readiness Scorecard with scores for backups, MFA, endpoints, admin rights, and recovery readiness.
List the prioritized hardening steps with owner, effort, and risk reduction for each (test restore first, then MFA, then local admin removal).
Document the backup state explicitly: exists/runs/off-site/tested, with the restore-test gap called out as the top finding.
Include the recovery documentation status and what the customer should have in place.
Security rule: never store backup credentials, recovery codes, or keys in the deliverables.
qa: Verify all whatIsIncluded items: backup assessment (exists/runs/off-site/tested), MFA review, endpoint protection and patch review, local admin review, recovery documentation and incident-readiness check, and the scorecard with hardening steps.
Confirm the backup findings clearly separate 'configured' from 'verified' (a configured-but-untested backup is the key gap).
Confirm the review was read-only.
Secret audit: confirm no backup credentials or keys appear in deliverables.
Flag follow-ups: restore-test scheduling, MFA enforcement, local admin removal, and the backup setup/upgrade recommendation.
closeout: Send the deliverables package: scorecard and hardening steps; complete the walkthrough.
Recommend next steps: backup setup or upgrade with a restore test, mfa_enforcement_project, endpoint_protection_rollout, and local_admin_removal_project.
Revoke any temporary access granted.
Record internal notes: readiness baseline and findings pointers.
Schedule a 60-day follow-up to confirm the top hardening steps were completed.

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the Nonprofit Cyber Readiness Review, understand the organization type (church, nonprofit, community org) from intake, and schedule the review with the lead admin or volunteer coordinator.
Send prep instructions: the organization should confirm who manages accounts, how online giving/payments are handled, and how volunteers get access.
Pre-work: prepare the budget-aware checklist (email/MFA, backup, volunteer access, giving platforms, staff practices) and note free/low-cost tool options.
Run the review: assess email security and MFA, backup posture, volunteer account management, online giving platform security, and staff security awareness practices.
Score and document: produce the readiness findings with budget-aware recommendations, prioritizing free and low-cost options.
Walk through the findings with the leadership contact: explain the risks in plain English and prioritize actions within the organization's budget.
Deliver the closeout package: the readiness report, the budget-aware action list, and recommended free/low-cost tool setup (e.g., free MFA, free backup tier).

triage: Confirm scope is the Nonprofit Cyber Readiness Review and the organization type; if they report an active incident, escalate accordingly.
Identify the lead admin or volunteer coordinator and confirm which platforms hold data (email, giving, donor records, files).
Gather baseline: platform list, user/volunteer counts, backup state, giving platform, and budget constraints that shape recommendations.

Create the ticket with product id nonprofit_cyber_readiness_review, expected deliverables (readiness report, budget-aware actions), exclusions (no changes), and assign a technician who understands nonprofit constraints.
Check prerequisites: review session booked and confirmation the organization is comfortable sharing its tooling and budget limits.
delivery: Email and MFA review: check email platform, MFA coverage on mailboxes and admin accounts, and SPF/DKIM/DMARC basics; flag accounts without MFA.
Backup assessment: confirm backup exists, runs, and is off-site; check whether restores were tested; note the free-tier options that fit the org.
Volunteer account review: inventory volunteer accounts and access, identify stale accounts, and check how access is granted and removed as volunteers turn over.
Online giving and payment platform check: review the giving platform's security settings, MFA on the finance account, and how donation data is stored.
Staff/volunteer awareness review: assess current practices (password sharing, phishing awareness, device handling) through discussion.
Recommendations: list actions with free/low-cost options prioritized first (free MFA, free backup, free phishing resources), then paid options.
Technical verification: confirm findings are evidence-backed, no changes were made, and donor/personal data was not captured.
documentation: Produce the readiness report: findings per area (email/MFA, backup, volunteers, giving, awareness) with plain-English impact for a nontechnical audience.
Include the budget-aware action list with cost tiers (free, low-cost, paid) and the recommended priority order.
Document volunteer account hygiene findings without listing personal email addresses where avoidable.
Include the giving-platform security notes and donor-data handling recommendations.
Security rule: never store donor lists, payment data, credentials, or volunteer personal data in the deliverables.
qa: Verify all whatIsIncluded items: email/MFA review, backup assessment, volunteer account review, giving platform check, staff awareness review, and budget-aware recommendations with free/low-cost options.
Confirm recommendations are realistic for a nonprofit budget and not just enterprise-grade tools.
Confirm the review was read-only.
Secret audit: confirm no donor data, credentials, or personal data appear in deliverables.
Flag follow-ups: MFA on the finance/giving account, volunteer account cleanup, and the backup setup with a free tier.
closeout: Send the deliverables package: readiness report and budget-aware action list.
Recommend next steps: volunteer_account_cleanup, guest_wi_fi_for_churches if applicable, or the church_it_foundation for a broader technology foundation.
Revoke any temporary access granted.
Record internal notes: org profile, platform list, and readiness baseline for future work.
Schedule a 90-day follow-up to review progress within the org's budget.

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the Vendor Access Review, and schedule the review with the admin who manages vendor relationships and system access.
Send prep instructions: customer should compile the vendor list (IT providers, accountants, marketing, remote-support vendors), their known system access, and any shared credentials.
Pre-work: prepare the vendor access inventory template and the remote-access review checklist (VPN, RDP, remote support tools).

Run the review: inventory all vendor accounts and their system access, review shared/generic vendor credentials, map remote-access paths, review the vendor offboarding process, and identify stale vendor accounts.
Build the Vendor Access Map: document each vendor, what they can access, how they access it, and whether access is still needed.
Walk through the map with the customer: confirm which vendors still need access and which should be revoked.
Deliver the closeout package: the Vendor Access Map, the prioritized cleanup plan (with revoke list approved by the customer), and the recommended access-review cadence.

triage: Confirm scope is the Vendor Access Review and that the customer will approve any access changes; if a vendor is under investigation, note it and avoid changing their access until cleared.
Verify admin access to the platforms where vendors hold accounts and confirm who manages vendor relationships.
Gather baseline: vendor list from the customer, known shared credentials, remote-access tools, and the current offboarding process.
Create the ticket with product id vendor_access_review, expected deliverables (Vendor Access Map, cleanup plan), and assign a technician.
Check prerequisites: vendor list compiled and approval workflow defined.
delivery: Vendor account inventory: enumerate vendor accounts across M365, cloud apps, hosting, remote-support tools, and any shared logins; record what each vendor can access.
Shared/generic credential review: identify generic vendor logins (shared admin, maintenance accounts) and assess the risk of shared credentials.
Remote-access path review: map how each vendor connects (VPN, RDP, remote-support sessions like ScreenConnect/TeamViewer), and verify MFA on each path where supported.
Offboarding process review: assess whether the customer has a defined process for removing vendor access when a relationship ends.
Stale vendor identification: flag vendors with no recent activity, no owner, or known-ended relationships whose access should be revoked.
Build the Vendor Access Map: vendor, systems accessed, access method, owner, last activity, and needed/not-needed status.
Technical verification: confirm the map is complete and accurate and that no changes were made without approval.
documentation: Produce the Vendor Access Map: vendor, systems, access method, owner, and status, as the primary deliverable.
Produce the prioritized cleanup plan: vendors to revoke (with the customer's approval), vendors to reduce access, and vendors to keep, each with action and owner.
Document the shared-credential risks found and the recommended remediation (named individual accounts, password rotation).
Include the recommended access-review cadence (quarterly) and the offboarding checklist the customer should adopt.
Security rule: never store vendor passwords, session tokens, or remote-access keys in the deliverables.
qa: Verify all whatIsIncluded items: vendor account inventory, shared credential review, remote-access path review, offboarding process review, stale vendor identification, and the Vendor Access Map with cleanup plan.
Confirm the cleanup plan distinguishes approved revokes from recommendations needing customer approval.
Confirm the review was read-only (no changes executed without approval).
Secret audit: confirm no vendor credentials appear in deliverables.
Flag follow-ups: revokes to execute, shared-credential rotation, and the offboarding process adoption.
closeout: Send the deliverables package: Vendor Access Map and cleanup plan; walk through the revoke list and obtain approval.
Recommend next steps: executing the approved revokes (as a follow-on), the admin_privilege_review if privileged vendor accounts exist, and the quarterly review cadence.
Revoke any temporary access granted for the review.
Record internal notes: vendor inventory baseline and the approved cleanup plan.
Schedule a quarterly reminder for the access review cadence.

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the Admin Privilege Review, define the in-scope platforms (M365, servers, cloud apps), and schedule the review with the admin who can approve role changes.
Send prep instructions: customer should confirm who holds privileged roles, which are needed, and their break-glass/emergency access approach.
Pre-work: prepare the privileged-account enumeration queries for M365, servers, and cloud apps, and stage the role-mapping template.

Run the review: inventory high-privilege accounts, compare role assignments against actual job responsibilities, identify excessive/stale/shared privileged accounts, and review the break-glass account.
Build the least-privilege roadmap: propose the role changes needed, with the documented approvals required for each.
Walk through the roadmap with the customer: confirm the proposed role changes and obtain approval to proceed (changes are a separate follow-on unless approved in scope).
Deliver the closeout package: the privileged account inventory, role assignment review, and the least-privilege remediation roadmap with documented approvals.

triage: Confirm scope is the Admin Privilege Review and whether role changes are in scope or review-only; if changes are not pre-approved, deliver the roadmap for approval.
Verify admin access to M365, servers, and cloud apps; confirm the decision maker who approves privilege changes.
Gather baseline: current privileged accounts, role assignments, break-glass process, and any access reviews done before.
Create the ticket with product id admin_privilege_review, expected deliverables (inventory, roadmap, approvals), and assign a technician experienced with privileged access.
Check prerequisites: approval workflow defined and break-glass account confirmed functional.
delivery: M365 privilege inventory: enumerate Global Admins and all delegated admin roles (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Intune, Billing), recording each holder and role.
Server privilege inventory: list domain/enterprise/schema admin members and local admin groups on servers where accessible, noting service accounts versus people.
Cloud app privilege inventory: for in-scope cloud apps, list super-admins and delegated admins from each console.
Role-vs-job review: compare each privileged account against the person's actual role, and flag excessive access (e.g., a bookkeeper with Global Admin).
Excessive/stale/shared identification: flag privileged accounts that are stale, shared, or hold more access than the role needs.
Break-glass review: verify the emergency access account exists, is documented, is not used for daily work, and has a defined activation procedure.
Build the roadmap: for each account propose Keep / Demote / Remove with the required approval, mapped to the least-privilege principle.
Technical verification: confirm the inventory is complete, the roadmap is justified, and no changes were made beyond approved scope.
documentation: Produce the privileged account inventory: account, platform, role, owner, purpose, and last-activity, as the primary deliverable.
Produce the role-vs-job review showing where access exceeds responsibility.
Document the least-privilege remediation roadmap with the proposed change and approval status for each account.
Document the break-glass account review (existence, usage, activation procedure) without the actual password.
Security rule: never store privileged credentials, service account secrets, or recovery codes in the deliverables.
qa: Verify all whatIsIncluded items: high-privilege inventory, role assignment review, excessive/stale/shared identification, break-glass review, change-management process assessment, and least-privilege roadmap with documented approvals.
Confirm the roadmap changes are all approved by the decision maker before any execution.
Confirm the break-glass account is documented and functional.
Secret audit: confirm no privileged secrets appear in deliverables.
Flag follow-ups: approved changes to execute, quarterly re-review, and MFA on all privileged accounts.
closeout: Send the deliverables package: inventory, role review, roadmap, and approvals.
Recommend next steps: executing the approved role changes (follow-on), the mfa_enforcement_project for privileged accounts, and the quarterly review cadence.
Revoke any temporary access granted.
Record internal notes: privilege baseline and approved roadmap.
Schedule a quarterly review reminder for the privileged access cadence.

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope and schedule: confirm the MFA Enforcement Project, define the systems in scope (M365, third-party platforms), and schedule the rollout planning session with the admin.
Send prep instructions: customer should confirm user count, available authenticator devices, which systems must be covered, and any users needing alternate methods (hardware keys).
Pre-work: prepare the M365 Conditional Access policy design, the enrollment plan, and the third-party MFA enablement runbook per in-scope platform.

Run the rollout: assess MFA coverage, design and enforce the M365 Conditional Access policy, create the user enrollment plan with step-by-step instructions, and enable MFA on critical third-party platforms.
Support enrollment: guide users through enrollment in small groups, handle lockout prevention (break-glass, backup methods), and fix any blocked users.
Verify and document: post-rollout verification that MFA applies to all users and admin actions, with evidence per system.
Deliver the closeout package: the enforcement policy documentation, the enrollment guide, the verification evidence, and the residual-platform list (systems still needing MFA).

triage: Confirm scope is the MFA Enforcement Project (broader rollout, not a single session); if the customer needs quick wins only, recommend mfa_setup_session instead.
Verify admin access to M365 and each in-scope platform; confirm the user list and enrollment approach.
Gather baseline: current MFA coverage per system, user count, devices, and any users who will need hardware keys or offline methods.

Create the ticket with product id mfa_enforcement_project, the in-scope systems, expected deliverables (policies, enrollment guide, verification), and assign a technician with Conditional Access experience.
Check prerequisites: rollout timeline agreed, enrollment windows scheduled, and break-glass account confirmed.
delivery: Coverage assessment: record current MFA state per system (M365, banking, payroll, CRM, registrar, etc.) and list every account and platform in scope.
M365 Conditional Access design: create the MCT-MFA-All-Users policy requiring MFA for all cloud apps and all users, excluding only the documented break-glass account.
Phased enforcement: enable the policy in report-only mode first, validate signals, then switch to on; apply to an admin pilot group before all users to catch issues early.
Third-party MFA enablement: walk through enabling MFA on each critical third-party platform with the admin, using the runbook for each platform's settings.
User enrollment plan: produce step-by-step instructions per staff member (which app, which accounts, recovery codes), and run small-group enrollment sessions.
Lockout prevention: ensure every user has a recovery method (backup codes, secondary device), the break-glass account is functional, and support is available for locked users.
Verification: test sign-in for each user on each covered system, confirm MFA prompts fire, and confirm admin actions also require MFA.
Technical verification: confirm coverage of every in-scope account, no business-blocking lockouts, and no recovery codes stored in MCT documentation.
